instructions: Grate the cheese on the large holes of a box grater. That should be about 2 cups.
Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Don't let it brown.
Add the cornmeal and stir. Turn the heat to low and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until it's lightly golden and smells toasty.
Add 1/2 cup water and stir until the cornmeal soaks it up and thickens.
Stir in the cheese over low heat until it melts and turns stringy.
Pour in 1/4 cup boiling water and cook, stirring, for about 2 minutes, until it's glossy and the butter rises to the top.
Taste it and stir in the salt if it needs it. Toast the bread.
Serve right away in warm bowls with the toast. It stiffens as it cools.
method_notes: Cooking Gorgeous leads (5 from 2 votes, under 20, so this is a fallback lead): butter, cornmeal toasted in it, a little water, then cheese melted in. Dobber Nation Loves agrees on the method and toasts the cornmeal dry first, with a larger ratio of cheese and kaymak. Kasseri stands in for Trabzon cheese. Bread is gluten-free to keep the tag.
